# Abstract

**Background and Aims:** Colonoscopy quality differs among endoscopists. We evaluated whether a structured training program improves adenoma detection.

**Methods:** We conducted a retrospective cohort study at three hospitals from 2015 to 2021.

**Results:** Among 4,812 colonoscopies, the adenoma detection rate increased from 28.1% to 35.2%.

**Conclusions:** The structured training program was associated with improved detection.

# Introduction

Colorectal cancer is the third most common cancer worldwide.[1] Adenoma detection rate (ADR) is the most important quality indicator.[2–4]

Several interventions have been proposed to improve ADR, but evidence remains limited.

# Methods

## Study design

This retrospective study was approved by the institutional review board (approval no. 2021-045).

## Outcomes

The primary outcome was ADR. Secondary outcomes included sessile serrated lesion detection rate and withdrawal time.

# Results

| Variable | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Colonoscopies, n | 2,201 | 2,611 |
| ADR, % | 28.1 | 35.2 |
| Withdrawal time, min | 7.2 | 8.4 |

![Figure 1. Withdrawal time by period and hospital.](../images/fig2_v2.png)

# Discussion

Our findings suggest that structured training improves ADR.

This study has several limitations. First, it was retrospective. Second, the endoscopists were aware of the study.
